description: The plot illustrates how accuracy-related metrics vary as a function of “Initial Confidence,” showing three series with error bars across the same set of confidence values. The x-axis is labeled “Initial Confidence,” uses a linear scale, and spans approximately 0.95 to 0.99 with ticks at 0.95, 0.96, 0.97, 0.98, and 0.99 (interval 0.01). The y-axis is labeled “Accuracy,” uses a linear scale, and ranges from 0.0 to 1.0 with labeled ticks at 0.0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, and 1.0 (interval 0.2). A blue solid line with circular markers (and vertical error bars) starts near 0.90 at 0.95, dips to about 0.86 at 0.96, rises to about 0.89 at 0.97, peaks around 0.93 at 0.98, and ends near 0.88 at 0.99. An orange dashed line with diamond markers labeled “Δ Acc” begins around 0.90 at 0.95, is about 0.86 at 0.96, increases to roughly 0.88 at 0.97, stays near 0.87 at 0.98, and declines to about 0.75 at 0.99, with error bars shown at each point. A green dash-dot line with square markers labeled “Initial Acc” lies near 0.00 at 0.95 and 0.96, is around 0.01 at 0.97, increases to about 0.05 at 0.98, and reaches roughly 0.13 at 0.99, also with vertical error bars.
